title.zh: 卷十二 列傳第六: 胡穎 徐度 杜稜 沈恪
title.en: Volume 12: Hu Ying; Xu Du; Du Leng; Shen Ke
title.raw: 卷十二 列傳第六: 胡穎 徐度 杜稜 沈恪 Volume 12: Hu Ying; Xu Du; Du Leng; Shen Ke

sentences.zh: 陳書卷十二

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 12
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 12

sentences.zh: 列傳第六

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Six
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Six

sentences.zh: 胡穎 徐度 子敬成 杜稜 沈恪

translations.literal: Hu Ying; Xu Du; son Jingcheng; Du Leng; Shen Ke
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying; Xu Du; son Jingcheng; Du Leng; Shen Ke

sentences.zh: 胡穎字方秀，吳興東遷人也。

translations.literal: Hu Ying, styled Fangxiu, was a native of Dongqian in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying, styled Fangxiu, came from Dongqian in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 其先寓居吳興，土斷為民。

translations.literal: His forebears had sojourned in Wuxing; when the native register was discontinued they were accounted local people.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Wuxing as sojourners; after the register was broken off they were reckoned natives of the place.

sentences.zh: 穎偉姿容，性寬厚。

translations.literal: Ying had a grand bearing and handsome looks, and a generous disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was tall and striking, with an open, generous nature.

sentences.zh: 梁世仕至武陵國侍郎，東宮直前。

translations.literal: Under Liang he rose to Vice-Minister in the state of Wuling and Direct Attendant Before the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as vice-minister in the state of Wuling and direct attendant before the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 出番禺，征討俚洞，廣州西江督護高祖在廣州，穎仍自結高祖，高祖與其同郡，接遇甚隆。

translations.literal: He went out from Panyu to campaign against the Li cave settlements. As West River defense commander of Guangzhou, when the Founder was at Guangzhou Ying attached himself to him of his own accord; the Founder was from the same commandery and received him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Posted from Panyu against the Li caves, he held the West River defense command at Guangzhou. When the Founder was there, Ying sought him out on his own. They shared a home commandery, and the Founder treated him with exceptional warmth.

sentences.zh: 及南征交趾，穎從行役，餘諸將帥皆出其下。

translations.literal: When the southern campaign against Jiaozhi was launched, Ying followed on campaign; the other generals all ranked below him.
translations.idiomatic: On the march to Jiaozhi he went with the army, and the other commanders stood beneath him in rank.

sentences.zh: 及平李賁，高祖旋師，穎隸在西江，出兵多以穎留守。

translations.literal: When Li Ben was pacified the Founder withdrew his army; Ying remained subordinate on the West River, and whenever troops marched out Ying was often left to hold the rear.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Ben fell the Founder turned homeward. Ying stayed on the West River, and in most campaigns he was left behind to guard the base.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，高祖克元景仲，仍渡嶺援臺，平蔡路養、李遷仕，穎皆有功。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder captured Yuan Jingzhong, then crossed the ranges to relieve the Terrace City, and pacified Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi; Ying had merit in all of this.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder took Yuan Jingzhong, crossed the mountains to relieve the capital, and crushed Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi. Ying earned merit in every fight.

sentences.zh: 歷平固、遂興二縣令。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of the two counties of Pinggu and Suixing.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Pinggu and Suixing.

sentences.zh: 高祖進軍頓西昌，以穎為巴丘縣令，鎮大皋，督糧運。

translations.literal: When the Founder advanced his army and halted at Xichang, he made Ying magistrate of Baqiu, garrisoned Dago, and supervised grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched and camped at Xichang, he made Ying magistrate of Baqiu, posted him at Dago, and put him in charge of grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 下至豫章，以穎監豫章郡。

translations.literal: Descending to Yuzhang, he made Ying overseer of Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Moving downriver to Yuzhang, he appointed Ying overseer of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖率眾與王僧辯會於白茅灣，同討侯景，以穎知留府事。

translations.literal: The Founder led his host to meet Wang Sengbian at Baimao Bay to campaign jointly against Hou Jing, and put Ying in charge of affairs left at headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder took his army to Baimao Bay to join Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing and left Ying to manage headquarters.

sentences.zh: 梁承聖初，元帝授穎假節、鐵騎將軍、羅州刺史，封漢陽縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang Chengsheng, Emperor Yuan granted Ying acting credentials, made him Iron Cavalry General and Inspector of Luo, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Hanyang county with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Liang Chengsheng, Emperor Yuan gave Ying acting credentials, made him iron cavalry general and inspector of Luo, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Hanyang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋除豫章內史，隨高祖鎮京口。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Interior Minister of Yuzhang and followed the Founder to garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became interior minister of Yuzhang and followed the Founder to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 齊遣郭元建出關，都督侯瑱率師禦之。

translations.literal: Qi sent Guo Yuanjian out through the pass, and Area Commander Hou Tian led troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Guo Yuanjian through the pass; Hou Tian led an army to meet him.

sentences.zh: 高祖選府內驍勇三千人配穎，令隨瑱，於東關大破之（元建）。[1]

translations.literal: The Founder selected three thousand brave men from his headquarters and assigned them to Ying, ordering him to follow Tian; at Dongguan they greatly defeated him, Yuanjian.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder picked three thousand brave men from his staff troops and assigned them to Ying under Tian. At Dongguan they routed Yuanjian.

sentences.zh: 三年，高祖圍廣陵，齊人東方光據宿預請降，[2]以穎為五原太守，隨杜僧明援光，不克，退還，除曲阿令。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Founder besieged Guangling. The Qi man Dongfang Guang held Suyu and asked to surrender; Ying was made Administrator of Wuyuan and followed Du Sengming to aid Guang, but they could not prevail, withdrew, and he was made Magistrate of Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the Founder besieged Guangling. Dongfang Guang of Qi held Suyu and asked to surrender; Ying was made administrator of Wuyuan and sent with Du Sengming to aid him. They failed, withdrew, and Ying was made magistrate of Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 尋領馬軍，從高祖襲王僧辯。

translations.literal: Soon he commanded cavalry and followed the Founder in the attack on Wang Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took command of cavalry and followed the Founder against Wang Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 又隨周文育於吳興討杜龕。

translations.literal: He also followed Zhou Wenyu in campaigning against Du Kan at Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Zhou Wenyu against Du Kan at Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，除假節、都督南豫州諸軍事、輕車將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai, he was appointed acting with credentials, Area Commander over military affairs in South Yuzhou, Light Chariot General, and Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 1, he received acting credentials and was made commander of South Yuzhou military affairs, light chariot general, and inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，除持節、散騎常侍、仁威將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, and Benevolent-Power General.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping year 1, he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and benevolent-power general.

sentences.zh: 尋兼丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，兼左衛將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Ying concurrently became Left Guard General; his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder accepted the abdication, Ying also became left guard general, retaining his other posts.

sentences.zh: 永定三年，隨侯安都征王琳，於宮亭破賊帥常眾愛等。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongding, he followed Hou Andu in campaigning against Wang Lin and defeated the rebel commanders Chang Zhongai and others at Gongting.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 3, he followed Hou Andu against Wang Lin and defeated the rebel commanders Chang Zhongai and others at Gongting.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，除侍中、都督吳州諸軍事、宣惠將軍、吳州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ying was appointed Palace Attendant, Area Commander over military affairs in Wuzhou, General Who Spreads Grace, and Inspector of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ying was made palace attendant, commander of Wuzhou military affairs, general who spreads grace, and inspector of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 不行，尋為義興太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post, and soon became Administrator of Yixing, retaining his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: He did not go to the post and was soon made administrator of Yixing, keeping his general rank.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，除散騎常侍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, he was appointed Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1, he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 其年六月卒，時年五十四。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth month of that year, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died that sixth month, aged fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、中護軍，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant and Central Protector of the Army, with the posthumous name Valiant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and central protector of the army and given the posthumous name Valiant.

sentences.zh: 二年，配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was enshrined in the Founder's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was given a place in the Founder's temple.

sentences.zh: 子六同嗣。

translations.literal: His son Liutong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liutong inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 穎弟鑠，亦隨穎將軍。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Shuo also followed Ying as a general.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Shuo followed him into the ranks as a general.

sentences.zh: 穎卒，鑠統其眾。

translations.literal: When Ying died, Shuo took command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, Shuo inherited his command.

sentences.zh: 歷東海、豫章二郡守，遷員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He served successively as administrator of the two commanderies of Donghai and Yuzhang, and was promoted to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Donghai and Yuzhang in turn, then rose to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 隨章昭達南平歐陽紇，[3]為廣州東江督護。

translations.literal: He followed Zhang Zhaoda in the southern pacification of Ouyang He, and was made East River defense commander of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south with Zhang Zhaoda to crush Ouyang He [3] and was made East River defense commander of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還預北伐，除雄信將軍、歷陽太守。

translations.literal: Returning, he took part in the northern campaign and was made Trustworthy-Faith General and Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Back from the south he joined the northern campaign and was appointed trustworthy-faith general and administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 太建六年卒，贈桂州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taijian he died; posthumously he was given Inspector of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taijian year 6 (574) and was posthumously made inspector of Gui.

sentences.zh: 徐度字孝節，安陸人也。

translations.literal: Xu Du, styled Xiaojie, was a native of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Du, styled Xiaojie, came from Anlu.

sentences.zh: 世居京師。

translations.literal: For generations his family dwelt in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived in the capital for generations.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，不拘小節。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and free, heedless of small proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was reckless and bold, careless of petty rules.

sentences.zh: 及長，姿貌瑰偉，嗜酒好博，恆使僮僕屠酤為事。

translations.literal: When grown, his looks were magnificent; he loved wine and gambling and constantly set his servants to butchering and brewing for his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he was imposing in bearing, fond of wine and dice, and kept servants busy slaughtering and brewing for his table.

sentences.zh: 梁始興內史蕭介之郡，度從之，將領士卒，征諸山洞，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: When Xiao Jie of Liang was interior minister of Shixing and went to his commandery, Du followed him, leading troops in campaigns against the mountain caves, and won a name for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's interior minister of Shixing, Xiao Jie, took up his post, Du went with him, commanding men against the hill tribes, and became known for daring.

sentences.zh: 高祖征交趾，厚禮招之，度乃委質。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Jiaozhi he treated Du with generous courtesy to win him; Du then offered his allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jiaozhi campaign the Founder courted him with rich gifts; Du at last pledged himself.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，高祖克定廣州，平蔡路養，破李遷仕，計畫多出於度。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder secured Guangzhou, pacified Cai Luyang, and broke Li Qianshi; much of the planning came from Du.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rising the Founder held Guangzhou, crushed Cai Luyang, and routed Li Qianshi. Du supplied much of the strategy.

sentences.zh: 兼統兵甲，每戰有功。

translations.literal: He also took overall command of armor and weapons; in every battle he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded the armorers and fought with merit in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 歸至白茅灣，梁元帝授寧朔將軍、合州刺史。

translations.literal: Returning to Baimao Bay, Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him Pacifying-the-North General and Inspector of He.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Baimao Bay, Emperor Yuan of Liang made him pacifying-the-north general and inspector of He.

sentences.zh: 侯景平後，追錄前後戰功，加通直散騎常侍，封廣德縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, his earlier and later battle achievements were entered in the record; he was promoted to direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hou Jing fell, past and recent victories were tallied. He was raised to direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮朱方，除信武將軍、蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: When the Founder garrisoned Zhufang, Du was appointed Trustworthy-Martial General and Administrator of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder held Zhufang, Du was made trustworthy-martial general and administrator of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣衡陽獻王平荊州，度率所領從焉。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Prince Xian of Hengyang to pacify Jingzhou, and Du led his own command in following him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Prince Xian of Hengyang to pacify Jingzhou, and Du went with him at the head of his troops.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，閒行東歸。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he traveled secretly back east.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, he slipped back east by hidden paths.

sentences.zh: 高祖平王僧辯，度與侯安都為水軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder pacified Wang Sengbian, Du and Hou Andu served as the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder struck Wang Sengbian, Du and Hou Andu commanded the river forces.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，高祖東討杜龕，奉敬帝幸京口，以度領宿衛，并知留府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai, when the Founder went east to campaign against Du Kan, he escorted Emperor Jing to Jingkou and had Du command the palace guard and manage affairs left at headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 1, the Founder marched east against Du Kan and escorted Emperor Jing to Jingkou; Du was put over the palace guard and left in charge of headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約等來寇，高祖與敬帝還都。

translations.literal: Xu Siwei, Ren Yue, and others came to raid; the Founder and Emperor Jing returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Siwei, Ren Yue, and others struck at the capital. The Founder and Emperor Jing came back to defend it.

sentences.zh: 時賊已據石頭城，市鄽居民，並在南路，去臺遙遠，恐為賊所乘，乃使度將兵鎮于冶城寺，築壘以斷之。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels already held Shitou citadel; market towns and residents along the southern road lay far from the Terrace City, and there was fear they would be seized by the rebels; Du was therefore sent with troops to garrison Yecheng Temple and build a stockade to cut them off.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels already held Shitou. Markets and towns on the southern road lay far from the palace, open to being overrun, so Du was sent with troops to Yecheng Temple to build a wall and block the approach.

sentences.zh: 賊悉眾來攻，不能克。

translations.literal: The rebels mustered their full strength to attack but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw their whole force against him and failed to break through.

sentences.zh: 高祖尋亦救之，大敗約等。

translations.literal: The Founder soon came to the rescue as well and inflicted a great defeat on Ren Yue and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder soon arrived in relief and routed Ren Yue and his allies.

sentences.zh: 明年，嗣徽等又引齊寇濟江，度隨眾軍破之於北郊壇。

translations.literal: The next year Siwei and the others again brought Northern Qi raiders across the river; Du followed the mass of armies and defeated them at the North Suburbs altar.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Siwei again drew Qi troops across the Yangzi. Du marched with the main host and beat them at the North Suburbs altar.

sentences.zh: 以功除信威將軍、郢州刺史，兼領吳興太守。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Trustworthy-Power General and Inspector of Ying, and concurrently Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made trustworthy-power general and inspector of Ying, and also administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 尋遷鎮右將軍、領軍將軍、徐州緣江諸軍事、[4]鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Suppressing-the-Right General, Commandant of the Guards, Commander of Military Affairs along the Yangzi bank of Xuzhou, Suppressing-the-North General, and Inspector of South Xuzhou, and was given one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made suppressing-the-right general, commandant of the guards, commander along the Yangzi frontier of Xuzhou, [4] suppressing-the-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou, with a full set of pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 周文育、侯安都等西討王琳，敗績，為琳所拘，乃以度為前軍都督，鎮于南陵。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wenyu, Hou Andu, and the others campaigned west against Wang Lin, they were defeated and detained by Lin, so Du was made Commander of the Vanguard Army and stationed at Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyu, Hou Andu, and the others marched west against Wang Lin, were defeated, and were held by him. Du was therefore made vanguard commander and posted at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，遷侍中、中撫軍將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Du was transferred to Palace Attendant, Central Pacifying General, and office holder with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and his title was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Du became palace attendant, central pacifying general, and holder of office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and his noble rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 未拜，出為使持節、散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Before he was formally installed, he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff with Credentials, Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, General Who Guards the East, and Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before formal installation, he was sent out with credentials as scattered-cavalry regular attendant, general who guards the east, and administrator of Wu.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1, one thousand households were added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 以平王琳功，改封湘東郡公，邑四千戶。

translations.literal: For his merit in pacifying Wang Lin, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangdong commandery with a fief of four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For helping pacify Wang Lin, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangdong commandery with four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，為侍中、中軍將軍。

translations.literal: When his term was complete, he became Palace Attendant and General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term, he became palace attendant and general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、都督會稽東陽臨海永嘉新安新寧信安晉安建安九郡諸軍事、鎮東將軍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff with Credentials, Area Commander over military affairs in the nine commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xin'an, Xinning, Xin'an, Jin'an, and Jian'an, General Who Guards the East, and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out with credentials as commander of the nine commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xin'an, Xinning, Xin'an, Jin'an, and Jian'an, general who guards the east, and administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 未行而太尉侯瑱薨于湘州，乃以度代瑱為都督湘沅武巴郢桂六州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Before he departed, Grand Commandant Hou Tian died in Xiangzhou, so Du was sent in Tian's place as Area Commander over military affairs in the six provinces of Xiang, Yuan, Wu, Ba, Ying, and Gui, General Who Guards the South, and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, Grand Commandant Hou Tian died in Xiangzhou. Du replaced him as commander of Xiang, Yuan, Wu, Ba, Ying, and Gui, general who guards the south, and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，為侍中、中軍大將軍，儀同、鼓吹並如故。

translations.literal: When his term was complete, he became Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Central Army; his equal-ceremony rank and pipes and drums remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term, he became palace attendant and grand general of the central army, retaining his equal-ceremony honors and pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，度預顧命，以甲仗五十人入殿省。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, Du was named in the final testament; fifty men with arms and armor entered the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, Du was named in the deathbed testament. Fifty armed guards were posted in the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，進位司空。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Du was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Du was promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 華皎據湘州反，引周兵下至沌口，與王師相持，乃加度使持節、車騎將軍，總督步軍，自安成郡由嶺路出于湘東，以襲湘州，盡獲其所留軍人家口以歸。

translations.literal: Hua Jiao held Xiangzhou in rebellion and brought Zhou troops down to Chun Ford, where they faced the royal army in stalemate; Du was then given credentials, made Chariots-and-Cavalry General, and put in overall command of the infantry. From Ancheng commandery he took the ridge route out into eastern Xiang to strike Xiangzhou and brought back all the army households and dependents Jiao had left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao rebelled in Xiangzhou and drew Zhou armies to Chun Ford, where they locked with the imperial host. Du was given credentials as chariots-and-cavalry general and made commander of all foot troops. He marched from Ancheng over the ridges into eastern Xiang, raided Xiangzhou, and carried off every soldier's family Jiao had left there.

sentences.zh: 光大二年薨，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangda he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangda year 2 (567), aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，給班劍二十人，諡曰忠肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Commandant, twenty ritual swords, and the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand commandant, granted twenty ritual swords, and given the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was given a place in the Founder's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4 (572) he was enshrined in the Founder's temple.

sentences.zh: 子敬成嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jingcheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingcheng inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 敬成幼聰慧，好讀書，少機警，善占對，結交文義之士，以識鑒知名。

translations.literal: Jingcheng was intelligent from childhood, loved reading, was alert and quick-witted in youth, skilled in replies, and associated with men of letters and principle; he was known for discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Jingcheng was bright from childhood and fond of books. In youth he was quick, sharp in replies, and moved among men of letters and principle, winning a reputation for discernment.

sentences.zh: 起家著作郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Gentleman for Compositions.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as gentleman for compositions.

sentences.zh: 永定元年，領度所部士卒，隨周文育、侯安都征王琳，於沌口敗績，為琳所縶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongding, he commanded Du's troops and followed Zhou Wenyu and Hou Andu in campaigning against Wang Lin; they were defeated at Dunkou, and he was bound by Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 1, he led his father's troops under Zhou Wenyu and Hou Andu against Wang Lin. They were defeated at Dunkou, and Lin took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 二年，隨文育、安都得歸，除太子舍人，遷洗馬。

translations.literal: In the second year, he returned with Wenyu and Andu, was appointed Crown Prince's Attendant, and was transferred to Xima.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he returned with Wenyu and Andu, became a crown prince's attendant, and was promoted to xima.

sentences.zh: （敬成父）度為吳郡太守，[5]以敬成監郡。

translations.literal: When Du, Jingcheng's father, was Administrator of Wu commandery, Jingcheng was made overseer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Du was administrator of Wu, Jingcheng was left to supervise the commandery.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，遷太子中舍人，拜湘東郡公世子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjia, he was transferred to Inner Attendant of the Crown Prince and invested as heir to the Duke of Xiangdong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 2, he became inner attendant to the crown prince and was invested as heir to the Duke of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 四年，度自湘州還朝，士馬精銳，敬成盡領其眾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Du returned to court from Xiangzhou, his soldiers and horses were elite, and Jingcheng took command of all of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Du returned from Xiangzhou with elite troops and horses, and Jingcheng took command of the whole force.

sentences.zh: 隨章昭達征陳寶應，晉安平，除貞威將軍、豫章太守。

translations.literal: He followed Zhang Zhaoda in campaigning against Chen Baoying; when Jin'an was pacified, he was appointed Upright-Power General and Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhang Zhaoda against Chen Baoying. After Jin'an was pacified, he was made upright-power general and administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 光大元年，華皎謀反，以敬成為假節、都督巴州諸軍事、雲旗將軍、巴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangda, when Hua Jiao plotted rebellion, Jingcheng was made acting with credentials, Area Commander over military affairs in Bazhou, Cloud-Banner General, and Inspector of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangda year 1, when Hua Jiao plotted rebellion, Jingcheng received acting credentials and became commander of Bazhou military affairs, cloud-banner general, and inspector of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 尋詔為水軍，隨吳明徹征華皎，皎平還州。

translations.literal: Soon an edict made him part of the naval forces; he followed Wu Mingche in campaigning against Hua Jiao, and when Jiao was pacified, he returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned to the fleet. He followed Wu Mingche against Hua Jiao and returned to his province after Jiao was crushed.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian, he left office because of mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 2, he left office for his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 尋起為持節、都督南豫州諸軍事、壯武將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander over military affairs in South Yuzhou, Stalwart-Martial General, and Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as bearer of the staff, commander of South Yuzhou military affairs, stalwart-martial general, and inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，襲爵湘東郡公，授太子右衛率。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he inherited the title Duke of Xiangdong commandery and was appointed Right Guard Commander of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he inherited the dukedom of Xiangdong and was made right guard commander of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 五年，除貞威將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Upright-Power General and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made upright-power general and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 其年隨都督吳明徹北討，出秦郡，別遣敬成為都督，乘金翅自歐陽引埭上泝江由廣陵。

translations.literal: That year he followed the commander-in-chief Wu Mingche on the northern campaign, marching out of Qin commandery; Jingcheng was separately dispatched as commander, taking the Golden Wings from Ouyangyin Dam upriver by way of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: That year he marched north under Wu Mingche, leaving from Qin commandery. Jingcheng was sent as a separate commander, sailing the Golden Wings from Ouyangyin Dam up the Yangzi through Guangling.

sentences.zh: 齊人皆城守，弗敢出。

translations.literal: The Qi men all held their cities and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces shut themselves in their walled towns and would not fight.

sentences.zh: 自繁梁湖下淮，圍淮陰城。

translations.literal: From Fanliang Lake he descended the Huai and besieged Huaiyin city.
translations.idiomatic: From Fanliang Lake he went down the Huai and laid siege to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 仍監北兗州。

translations.literal: He was then made overseer of North Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made overseer of North Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮、泗義兵相率響應，一二日間，眾至數萬，遂克淮陰、山陽、鹽城三郡，并連口、朐山二戍。

translations.literal: Righteous militia of Huai and Si rose in answer one after another; within a day or two their numbers reached tens of thousands; he then took the three commanderies of Huaiyin, Shanyang, and Yancheng, and the two garrisons of Lian Ford and Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal levies on the Huai and Si rallied to him by the thousand. In a day or two he had tens of thousands of men and seized Huaiyin, Shanyang, and Yancheng, with the garrisons at Lian Ford and Qushan.

sentences.zh: 仍進攻鬱州，克之。

translations.literal: He then advanced to attack Yuzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Yuzhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 以功加通直散騎常侍、雲旗將軍，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and Cloud-Banner General, and his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and cloud-banner general, with five hundred more households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 又進號壯武將軍，鎮朐山。

translations.literal: His title was further advanced to Stalwart-Martial General, and he garrisoned Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to stalwart-martial general and posted at Qushan.

sentences.zh: 坐於軍中輒科訂，并誅新附，免官。

translations.literal: Because in camp he arbitrarily imposed punishments and also executed newly submitted men, he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for summarily punishing men in camp and executing fresh recruits.

sentences.zh: 尋復為持節、都督安元潼三州諸軍事、安州刺史，將軍如故，鎮宿預。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made with credentials, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the three provinces of An, Yuan, and Tong, Inspector of An, general as before, garrisoning Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored with credentials as area commander of An, Yuan, and Tong, inspector of An, with his old rank, garrisoning Suyu.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，時年三十六。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍，諡曰思。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given scattered-cavalry regular attendant, with the posthumous title Reflective.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and given the posthumous name Reflective.

sentences.zh: 子敞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 杜稜字雄盛，吳郡錢塘人也。

translations.literal: Du Leng, styled Xiongsheng, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Leng, styled Xiongsheng, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 世為縣大姓。

translations.literal: For generations his clan was a great surname of the county.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his clan was one of the county's great families.

sentences.zh: 稜頗涉書傳，少落泊，不為當世所知。

translations.literal: Leng had dipped into books and records; in youth he was adrift and unknown to his age.
translations.idiomatic: Leng had read widely, but in youth he drifted without notice.

sentences.zh: 遂遊嶺南，事梁廣州刺史新渝侯蕭映。

translations.literal: He then traveled to Lingnan and served Liang's Inspector of Guangzhou, the Prince of Xinyu, Xiao Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He went south to Lingnan and entered the service of Liang's inspector of Guangzhou, the Prince of Xinyu, Xiao Ying.

sentences.zh: 映卒，從高祖，恆典書記。

translations.literal: When Ying died he followed the Founder and constantly kept the written records.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died he followed the Founder and served constantly as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，命稜將領，平蔡路養、李遷仕皆有功。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he was ordered to take command; pacifying Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi, he had merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he was put in command. He helped crush Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi and won merit in both campaigns.

sentences.zh: 軍至豫章，梁元帝承制授稜仁威將軍、石州刺史，上陌縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yuzhang, Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting on the regency commission, appointed Leng Benevolent-Power General and Inspector of Shi, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shangmo county with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuzhang, Emperor Yuan of Liang, exercising regency powers, made Leng benevolent-power general and inspector of Shi, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shangmo with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，高祖鎮朱方，稜監義興、琅邪二郡。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified and the Founder garrisoned Zhufang, Leng supervised the two commanderies of Yixing and Langya.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell and the Founder held Zhufang, Leng was put over Yixing and Langya.

sentences.zh: 高祖誅王僧辯，[6]引稜與侯安都等共議，稜難之。

translations.literal: When the Founder killed Wang Sengbian, he drew Leng, Hou Andu, and the others into the planning, but Leng objected.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder moved against Wang Sengbian, he brought Leng, Hou Andu, and the others into council; Leng resisted the plan.

sentences.zh: 高祖懼其泄己，乃以手巾絞稜，稜悶絕于地，因閉於別室。

translations.literal: The Founder feared he would reveal the matter, so he strangled Leng with a hand towel; Leng lost consciousness on the floor and was then shut in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Leng would leak the plan, the Founder strangled him with a hand towel. Leng collapsed unconscious and was locked in another room.

sentences.zh: 軍發，召與同行。

translations.literal: When the army set out, he summoned Leng to go with it.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched, he summoned Leng to accompany it.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯平後，高祖東征杜龕等，留稜與安都居守。

translations.literal: After Sengbian was pacified, the Founder campaigned east against Du Kan and the others, leaving Leng and Andu to hold the base.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengbian was defeated, the Founder marched east against Du Kan and left Leng and Andu to guard the base.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約引齊寇濟江，攻臺城，安都與稜隨方抗拒，稜晝夜巡警，綏撫士卒，未常解帶。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue brought Qi raiders across the river and attacked the Terrace City. Andu and Leng resisted them wherever needed; Leng patrolled day and night, soothed and encouraged the soldiers, and never even took off his belt.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue led Qi raiders across the river against the capital. Andu and Leng met them on every side; Leng patrolled day and night, steadied the men, and never once loosened his belt.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功除通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Right Guard General, and Intendant of Danyang for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, his merit brought him appointment as direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, right guard general, and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 永定元年，加侍中、忠武將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongding, he was additionally made Palace Attendant and Loyal-Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 1, he was also made palace attendant and loyal-martial general.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中領軍，侍中，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Central Commandant of the Guards, with Palace Attendant and his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became central commandant of the guards, retaining palace attendant and his general rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，高祖崩，世祖在南皖。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Founder died while Emperor Wen was at Southern Wan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the Founder died with Emperor Wen away at Southern Wan.

sentences.zh: 時內無嫡嗣，外有彊敵，侯瑱、侯安都、徐度等並在軍中，朝廷宿將，唯稜在都，獨典禁兵，乃與蔡景歷等祕不發喪，奉迎世祖，事見景歷傳。

translations.literal: At the time there was no legitimate heir inside the capital and powerful enemies outside; Hou Tian, Hou Andu, Xu Du, and the others were all with the armies, and among the court's veteran generals only Leng was in the capital, where he alone commanded the palace guards. He therefore joined Cai Jingli and the others in keeping the death secret and welcoming Emperor Wen; the matter is seen in Jingli's biography.
translations.idiomatic: There was no direct heir in the capital and strong enemies outside. Hou Tian, Hou Andu, Xu Du, and the rest were all in the field; of the court's old generals, only Leng was in the capital, commanding the guards. He and Cai Jingli kept the death secret and brought Emperor Wen in, as told in Jingli's biography.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，遷領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Leng was transferred to Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Leng became commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，以預建立之功，改封永城縣侯，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, for his merit in taking part in the enthronement, he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng county and his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1, for helping establish the new reign, he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng with five hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 出為雲麾將軍，晉陵太守，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Cloud-Banner General and Administrator of Jinling, with his salary raised to middle two thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as cloud-banner general and administrator of Jinling, with middle two-thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: 二年，徵為侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was summoned as Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was recalled as palace attendant and commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 尋遷翊左將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Assists the Left and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became general who assists the left and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，遷鎮右將軍、特進，侍中、尹如故。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, he was transferred to Suppressing-the-Right General and Special Grandee, palace attendant and metropolitan governor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he was made suppressing-the-right general and special grandee, retaining his posts as palace attendant and metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 光大元年，解尹，量置佐史，給扶，重授領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangda he was relieved of the governorship; a full staff of aides was appointed, supports were granted, and he was again given Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangda (567) he left the metropolitan post. A full staff was assigned, carriage supports granted, and he was again made commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，出為散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、吳興太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he went out as scattered-cavalry regular attendant, Suppressing-the-East General, and Administrator of Wuxing, with salary of middle two thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taijian (569) he was sent out as scattered-cavalry regular attendant, suppressing-the-east general, and administrator of Wuxing, at middle two-thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: 二年，徵為侍中、鎮右將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned to be palace attendant and Suppressing-the-Right General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled as palace attendant and suppressing-the-right general.

sentences.zh: 尋加特進、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was further given special grandee and Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made special grandee and protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 三年，以公事免侍中、護軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, on public business he was removed from palace attendant and protector of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was dismissed from palace attendant and protector of the army on official grounds.

sentences.zh: 四年，復為侍中、右光祿大夫，并給鼓吹一部，將軍、佐史、扶並如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again made palace attendant and Right Grandee for Splendid Virtue, and was also given one set of martial pipes and drums; general, staff, and supports were all as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned as palace attendant and right grandee for splendid virtue, with pipes and drums restored; his rank, staff, and carriage supports stayed as before.

sentences.zh: 稜歷事三帝，並見恩寵。

translations.literal: Leng served three emperors and in each was shown favor.
translations.idiomatic: Leng served three emperors and won favor under each.

sentences.zh: 末年不預征役，優遊京師，賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: In his last years he took no part in campaigns; he lived at ease in the capital, and gifts and rewards were generous.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years he stayed out of the field, idling in the capital while honors and gifts flowed freely.

sentences.zh: 頃之卒于官，時年七十。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，喪事所須，並令資給，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies; all funeral needs were ordered supplied, and his posthumous title was Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand master for splendid happiness with three-excellency honors; the court paid for the funeral and gave him the posthumous name Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 其年配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: That year he was given a place in the Founder's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was enshrined in the Founder's temple.

sentences.zh: 子安世嗣。

translations.literal: His son Anshi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anshi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 沈恪字子恭，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Ke, styled Zigong, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ke, styled Zigong, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 深沈有幹局。

translations.literal: He was deep and steady, with administrative capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was reserved and steady, with a gift for command.

sentences.zh: 梁新渝侯蕭映為郡將，召為主簿。

translations.literal: When Liang's Prince of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, was commandery general, Ke was summoned as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Prince of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, held a commandery, Ke was called up as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 映遷北徐州，恪隨映之鎮。

translations.literal: When Ying was transferred to North Xuzhou, Ke followed Ying to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying moved to North Xuzhou, Ke went with him to the post.

sentences.zh: 映遷廣州，以恪兼府中兵參軍，常領兵討伐俚洞。

translations.literal: When Ying was transferred to Guangzhou, Ke was made concurrent military adjutant in the establishment and constantly led troops to campaign against the Li cave settlements.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying went to Guangzhou, Ke was made concurrent military adjutant in the princely staff and often led troops against the Li caves.

sentences.zh: 盧子略之反也，恪拒戰有功，除中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Lu Zilüe rebelled, Ke resisted in battle and had merit; he was made middle military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zilüe rose, Ke fought him off with merit and was made middle military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 高祖與恪同郡，情好甚暱，蕭映卒後，高祖南討李賁，仍遣妻子附恪還鄉。

translations.literal: The Founder was from the same commandery and was on very close terms with Ke; after Xiao Ying died the Founder campaigned south against Li Ben and sent his wife and children home with Ke to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder shared Ke's home commandery and liked him well. After Xiao Ying died, on the march against Li Ben he sent his family home under Ke's escort.

sentences.zh: 尋補東宮直後，以嶺南勳除員外散騎侍郎，仍令招集宗從子弟。[7]

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Direct Attendant After the Eastern Palace; for his merit in Lingnan he was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry attendant gentleman and was further ordered to gather kinsmen and clan youths.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made direct attendant after the Eastern Palace, then brevetted scattered-cavalry attendant gentleman for his southern service and told to rally his clan.

sentences.zh: 侯景圍臺城，恪率所領入臺，隨例加右軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the Terrace City, Ke led his command into the city and, by precedent, was promoted to Right Army General.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Ke brought his men inside the walls and, by precedent, was made right army general.

sentences.zh: 賊起東西二土山以逼城，城內亦作土山以應之，恪為東土山主，晝夜拒戰。

translations.literal: The rebels raised eastern and western earthen hills to press the walls; within the city earthen hills were also built in answer; Ke was master of the eastern hill and fought off attacks day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels piled earthen mounts east and west against the walls; the defenders raised mounts of their own. Ke held the eastern mound and fought day and night.

sentences.zh: 以功封東興縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 京城陷，恪閒行歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Ke slipped away by hidden paths and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Ke stole home by back roads.

sentences.zh: 高祖之討侯景，遣使報恪，乃於東起兵相應。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Hou Jing he sent envoys to notify Ke; Ke then raised troops in the east in response.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent word when he marched against Hou Jing; Ke raised men in the east to join him.

sentences.zh: 賊平，恪謁高祖於京口，即日授都軍副。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Ke called on the Founder at Jingkou and that same day was appointed deputy commander of the capital army.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fell, Ke met the Founder at Jingkou and was named deputy commander of the capital army that same day.

sentences.zh: 尋為（君）府司馬。[8]

translations.literal: Soon he became marshal of the commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made marshal of the commander's office.

sentences.zh: 及高祖謀討王僧辯，恪預其謀。

translations.literal: When the Founder planned to campaign against Wang Sengbian, Ke took part in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder planned his move against Wang Sengbian, Ke was in the councils.

sentences.zh: 時僧辯女婿杜龕鎮吳興，高祖乃使世祖還長城，立柵備龕，又使恪還武康，招集兵眾。

translations.literal: At the time Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan garrisoned Wuxing, so the Founder sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to set up palisades against Kan, and also sent Ke back to Wukang to gather troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan then held Wuxing. The Founder sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to build defenses against him and sent Ke back to Wukang to raise men.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯誅，龕果遣副將杜泰率眾襲世祖於長城。

translations.literal: When Sengbian was killed, Kan indeed sent his deputy Du Tai to lead troops in attacking Emperor Wen at Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Sengbian was killed, Kan sent his deputy Du Tai to attack Emperor Wen at Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 恪時已率兵士出縣誅龕黨與，高祖尋遣周文育來援長城，文育至，泰乃遁走。

translations.literal: Ke had already led soldiers out of the county to punish Kan's followers; the Founder soon sent Zhou Wenyu to reinforce Changcheng, and when Wenyu arrived, Tai fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ke had already marched out to kill Kan's partisans. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyu to reinforce Changcheng, and once Wenyu arrived, Tai fled.

sentences.zh: 世祖仍與文育進軍出郡，恪軍亦至，屯于郡南。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen then advanced out of the commandery with Wenyu, and Ke's army also arrived and camped south of the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen and Wenyu advanced out of the commandery; Ke's army arrived as well and camped to the south.

sentences.zh: 及龕平，世祖襲東揚州刺史張彪，以恪監吳興郡。

translations.literal: After Kan was pacified, Emperor Wen attacked Zhang Biao, Inspector of East Yangzhou, and had Ke supervise Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Kan was defeated, Emperor Wen struck Zhang Biao, inspector of East Yangzhou, and left Ke over Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 太平元年，除宣猛將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, Ke was appointed Fierce-Proclaiming General and Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping year 1, Ke was made fierce-proclaiming general and inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 其年遷永嘉太守。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was transferred to Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 不拜，復令監吳興郡。

translations.literal: He was not installed, and was again ordered to supervise Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He did not take up the appointment and was again ordered to supervise Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 自吳興入朝。

translations.literal: From Wuxing he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: From Wuxing he came to court.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，使中書舍人劉師知引恪，令勒兵入辭，[9]因衛敬帝如別宮。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he had Secretariat Drafter Liu Shizhi bring Ke in and ordered him to lead troops in to take leave, then escort Emperor Jing to a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder accepted the abdication, he had Secretariat Drafter Liu Shizhi bring Ke in and ordered Ke to lead troops in for the farewell audience, then escort Emperor Jing to a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 恪乃排闥入見高祖，叩頭謝曰：「恪身經事蕭家來，今日不忍見許事，分受死耳，決不奉命。」

translations.literal: Ke pushed through the door to see the Founder, knocked his head to the ground, and apologized, saying, "This body of mine has served the Xiao house; today I cannot bear to see such a thing. I am prepared to accept death, but I will not obey the order."
translations.idiomatic: Ke forced his way in to the Founder, bowed his head to the floor, and said, "I have served the Xiao house with this body. I cannot bear to see this done today. I am ready to die, but I will not obey."

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其意，乃不復逼，更以盪主王僧志代之。

translations.literal: The Founder admired his intent and no longer pressed him, instead replacing him with assault leader Wang Sengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder admired his loyalty and did not press him further, replacing him with the assault leader Wang Sengzhi.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，除吳興太守。

translations.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, [Ke] was appointed Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Ke was made administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，徙監會稽郡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was transferred to supervise Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year two he was transferred to oversee Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 會余孝頃謀應王琳，出兵臨川攻周迪，以恪為壯武將軍，率兵踰嶺以救迪。

translations.literal: When Yu Xiaoqing plotted to join Wang Lin, he sent troops from Linchuan to attack Zhou Di; Ke was made Stalwart-Martial General and led troops across the ranges to rescue Di.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Xiaoqing plotted to side with Wang Lin and marched from Linchuan against Zhou Di, Ke was made stalwart-martial general and led an army over the mountains to relieve Di.

sentences.zh: 余孝頃聞恪至，退走。

translations.literal: When Yu Xiaoqing heard Ke had arrived, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Xiaoqing learned Ke was coming, he retreated.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷使持節、通直散騎常侍、智武將軍、吳州刺史，便道之鄱陽。

translations.literal: In year three he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Courier Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Intelligent-Martial General, and Inspector of Wu prefecture, and went by convenient route to Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was made bearer of the staff, courier scattered-cavalry regular attendant, intelligent-martial general, and inspector of Wu prefecture, and went by convenient route to Poyang.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔追還，行會稽郡事。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict recalling him; he acted in Kuaiji commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict recalled him, and he administered Kuaiji commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 其年，除散騎常侍、忠武將軍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Loyal-Martial General, and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, loyal-martial general, and administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，進督會稽、東陽、新安、臨海、永嘉、建安、晉安、新寧、信安九郡諸軍事，將軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ke was advanced to command military affairs in the nine commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, Yongjia, Jian'an, Jin'an, Xinning, and Xin'an; his generalship and administrator post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ke was promoted to command the nine commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, Yongjia, Jian'an, Jin'an, Xinning, and Xin'an, while keeping his general and administrator posts.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1, five hundred households were added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 二年，徵為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was summoned as Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he was recalled as left guard general.

sentences.zh: 俄出為都督郢武巴定四州諸軍事、軍師將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Area Commander over military affairs in the four provinces of Ying, Wu, Ba, and Ding, Army Adviser General, and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as commander of Ying, Wu, Ba, and Ding, army adviser general, and inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，徵為中護軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was summoned as Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was recalled as central protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 尋遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Protector General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became protector general.

sentences.zh: 光大二年，遷使持節、都督荊武祐三州諸軍事、平西將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangda, he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff with Credentials, Area Commander over military affairs in the three provinces of Jing, Wu, and You, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangda year 2, he was made bearer of the staff with credentials, commander of Jing, Wu, and You, general who pacifies the west, and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未之鎮，改為護軍將軍。[10]

translations.literal: Before he went to the garrison, he was changed to Protector General.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left for the post, he was reassigned as protector general.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，加散騎常侍、都督廣衡東衡交越成定新合羅愛德宜黃利安石雙等十八州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, [Ke] was additionally made Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the eighteen prefectures of Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, General Who Guards the South, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ke was further made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies in eighteen southern provinces including Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, general who guards the south, general who pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恪未至嶺，前刺史歐陽紇舉兵拒險，恪不得進，朝廷遣司空章昭達督眾軍討紇，紇平，乃得入州。

translations.literal: Before Ke reached the ranges, the former inspector Ouyang He raised troops blocking the passes; Ke could not advance. The court sent Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda to command the armies to campaign against He; when He was pacified, [Ke] was able to enter the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before Ke crossed the mountains, the former inspector Ouyang He held the passes with an army and blocked him. The court sent Zhang Zhaoda, minister of works, to lead the armies against He; only after He was suppressed could Ke enter the province.

sentences.zh: 州罹兵荒，所在殘毀，恪綏懷安緝，被以恩惠，嶺表賴之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had suffered war and devastation; everywhere was ruined. Ke soothed and settled the people, covering them with kindness; the region beyond the ranges relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: The province had been ravaged by war and lay in ruins. Ke comforted and settled the people, treating them with kindness, and the far south came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，徵為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian, he was summoned as Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4, he was recalled as commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 及代還，以途遠不時至，為有司所奏免。

translations.literal: When his replacement arrived and he returned, because the road was distant and he did not arrive on time, the responsible officials memorialized against him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When his successor arrived and he returned, the long road delayed him. Officials impeached him for not arriving on time, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十一年，起為散騎常侍、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was restored as Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, he was brought back as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and chamberlain for the guards.

sentences.zh: 其年授平北將軍、假節，監南兗州。

translations.literal: That year he was granted General Who Pacifies the North, acting credentials, and supervision of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was made general who pacifies the north, received acting credentials, and was put over South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改授散騎常侍、翊右將軍，監南徐州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was reassigned as Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and General Who Assists the Right, supervising South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, he was reassigned as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and general who assists the right, supervising South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又遣電威將軍裴子烈領馬五百匹，助恪緣江防戍。

translations.literal: The court also sent Lightning-Might General Pei Zilie with five hundred horses to assist Ke in the defenses and garrisons along the river.
translations.idiomatic: It also sent Pei Zilie, lightning-might general, with five hundred horses to help Ke defend the river line.

sentences.zh: 明年，入為衛尉卿，常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: The next year, he entered court as Chamberlain for the Guards, with Regular Attendant and generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, he returned to court as chamberlain for the guards, keeping regular attendant and his general rank.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中，遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Palace Attendant and transferred to Protector General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made palace attendant and promoted to protector general.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，以疾改授散騎常侍、特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord took the throne, because of illness Ke was reassigned as Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Special Grandee, and Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord succeeded, Ke was ill, so he was reassigned as scattered-cavalry regular attendant, special grandee, and grandee of splendid happiness with gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: He died that year, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈翊左將軍，詔給東園祕器，仍出舉哀，喪事所須，並令資給，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Assists the Left; an edict supplied a coffin from the Eastern Park imperial workshop, went out to hold mourning, and ordered all funeral needs funded; his posthumous name was Primal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who assists the left. The court supplied an Eastern Park coffin, held public mourning, paid all funeral costs, and gave him the posthumous name Primal.

sentences.zh: 子法興嗣。

translations.literal: His son Faxing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Faxing inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：胡穎、徐度、杜稜、沈恪並附騏驥而騰躍，依日月之光輝，始覯王佐之才，方悟公輔之量，生則肉食，終以配饗。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, and Shen Ke all attached to swift steeds and leaped upward, relied on the brilliance of sun and moon, first beheld the talent of royal assistants, then understood the measure of chief ministers; in life they ate at meat tables, in death they were granted temple shares.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, and Shen Ke all rode swift steeds to rise, drew on the light of sun and moon, first saw the gifts of royal counselors, then grasped the stature of chief ministers; in life they feasted at court, in death they shared offerings in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 盛矣哉！

translations.literal: Magnificent indeed!
translations.idiomatic: How splendid!
